title: Design Process
description: A structured design process that moves from understanding the context to defining problems, developing responses, testing alternatives, and refining the design.

children.label: Analysis
children.description: Understand the existing conditions, context, users, opportunities, and constraints that influence the design.

children.label: Site Analysis
children.description: Study the physical, environmental, spatial, and contextual characteristics of the site.

children.label: Physical Analysis
children.description: Study the physical characteristics and existing conditions of the site.

children.label: Topography
children.description: Understand levels, slopes, contours, depressions, and other terrain characteristics.

children.label: Existing Structures
children.description: Document buildings, walls, paving, utilities, structures, and other existing physical elements.

children.label: Access and Circulation
children.description: Study pedestrian, vehicular, service, emergency, and universal access routes.

children.label: Environmental Analysis
children.description: Understand environmental factors that affect comfort, ecology, and design performance.

children.label: Sun and Shadow
children.description: Study solar exposure, shade patterns, seasonal changes, and potential solar gains.

children.label: Wind Analysis
children.description: Study prevailing winds, ventilation opportunities, and areas of wind exposure.

children.label: Water and Drainage
children.description: Understand rainfall, surface runoff, drainage patterns, water accumulation, and infiltration.

children.label: Ecological Analysis
children.description: Study existing vegetation, habitats, biodiversity, ecological assets, and sensitive areas.

children.label: Spatial Analysis
children.description: Understand spatial structure, edges, connections, visibility, and relationships between spaces.

children.label: Spatial Structure
children.description: Identify major spaces, spatial hierarchy, enclosure, openness, and spatial sequences.

children.label: Visual Analysis
children.description: Study views, vistas, landmarks, visual connections, and important visual relationships.

children.label: Edge Analysis
children.description: Study boundaries, transitions, interfaces, barriers, and connections between adjacent areas.

children.label: User Analysis
children.description: Understand users, their needs, behaviours, activities, expectations, and patterns of use.

children.label: User Groups
children.description: Identify different user groups and their characteristics.

children.label: User Needs
children.description: Identify functional, social, physical, emotional, and accessibility needs.

children.label: User Behaviour
children.description: Understand how users move, interact, occupy, and use spaces over time.

children.label: Movement Patterns
children.description: Study pedestrian and other movement patterns through the site.

children.label: Activity Patterns
children.description: Study where, when, and how different activities occur.

children.label: Context Analysis
children.description: Understand the wider physical, social, cultural, regulatory, and urban context.

children.label: Urban Context
children.description: Study surrounding development, land uses, infrastructure, streets, and public spaces.

children.label: Social Context
children.description: Understand community characteristics, social relationships, local practices, and patterns of use.

children.label: Regulatory Context
children.description: Identify applicable regulations, standards, planning requirements, and design constraints.

children.label: Problem Definition
children.description: Convert analytical findings into clearly defined design problems, opportunities, and priorities.

children.label: Problem Identification
children.description: Identify gaps, conflicts, deficiencies, risks, and unmet needs revealed through analysis.

children.label: Functional Problems
children.description: Identify problems related to access, movement, use, capacity, and functionality.

children.label: Environmental Problems
children.description: Identify environmental weaknesses and opportunities for improvement.

children.label: User Problems
children.description: Identify problems experienced by different user groups.

children.label: Problem Magnitude
children.description: Assess the scale, severity, frequency, impact, and extent of identified problems.

children.label: Severity
children.description: Assess how serious the consequence of the problem is.

children.label: Frequency
children.description: Assess how frequently the problem occurs.

children.label: Impact
children.description: Assess the effect of the problem on users, environment, function, and design quality.

children.label: Prioritisation
children.description: Rank problems and opportunities according to their importance, urgency, impact, and feasibility.

children.label: Priority Ranking
children.description: Rank identified problems according to defined evaluation criteria.

children.label: Design Objectives
children.description: Translate prioritised problems into clear objectives that the design should address.

children.label: Ideation
children.description: Generate and develop possible design responses to the identified problems and opportunities.

children.label: Concept Generation
children.description: Generate multiple possible design concepts without prematurely selecting a single solution.

children.label: Spatial Concepts
children.description: Generate alternative spatial arrangements and organisational strategies.

children.label: Circulation Concepts
children.description: Generate alternative movement and circulation strategies.

children.label: Landscape Concepts
children.description: Generate landscape, planting, ecological, and open-space strategies.

children.label: Concept Development
children.description: Develop promising concepts into more coherent and testable design alternatives.

children.label: Spatial Development
children.description: Develop spatial relationships, hierarchy, proportions, and organisation.

children.label: Material and Character Development
children.description: Develop material, landscape, architectural, and visual character.

children.label: Technical Development
children.description: Develop technical feasibility, construction logic, infrastructure, and performance considerations.

children.label: Scenario Testing
children.description: Test design alternatives against different conditions, users, situations, and performance criteria.

children.label: User Scenarios
children.description: Test how different users experience and interact with the proposed design.

children.label: Environmental Scenarios
children.description: Test the design under different environmental and climatic conditions.

children.label: Time-Based Scenarios
children.description: Test how the design performs across different times of day, seasons, or phases of use.

children.label: Evaluation
children.description: Compare design alternatives and assess how effectively they respond to the defined objectives and problems.

children.label: Criteria-Based Evaluation
children.description: Evaluate alternatives against predefined design criteria and objectives.

children.label: Alternative Comparison
children.description: Compare the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and limitations of different alternatives.

children.label: Solution Selection
children.description: Select or combine the alternatives that best satisfy the design objectives.

children.label: Design Development
children.description: Develop the selected design direction into a coordinated and resolved proposal.

children.label: Spatial Resolution
children.description: Resolve spatial organisation, dimensions, circulation, hierarchy, and relationships.

children.label: Material Resolution
children.description: Resolve materials, finishes, planting, furniture, lighting, and visual character.

children.label: Technical Resolution
children.description: Resolve technical systems, construction details, drainage, services, and implementation requirements.

children.label: Final Review
children.description: Review the developed design against the original objectives, constraints, and identified problems.

children.label: Objective Check
children.description: Verify whether the final design responds adequately to the established design objectives.

children.label: Performance Check
children.description: Review functional, environmental, social, aesthetic, and technical performance.

children.label: Final Refinement
children.description: Make final adjustments based on the review before documenting the design.
